cards.title: Grounding through retrieval
cards.payload: RAG conditions generation on retrieved external material, but a research paper's specific dense index is not an HW1 implementation mandate. Homework's BM25 test is lexical and deterministic, while Lewis et al. use dense retrieval over Wikipedia; do not conflate these two architectures.

cards.title: Assignment truth outranks illustrative reading
cards.payload: Starter contracts and tests constrain this homework. MCP and dense RAG are transferable knowledge, not required implementation choices. Never silently substitute them for stated homework interfaces.

cards.title: Framework-free harness
cards.payload: Use the supplied plain chat-completion call and own code to implement required student-facing adapter behaviors while preserving provided types.

cards.title: Answer/support contract
cards.payload: Given a question and returned email search results, emit answer and support list referencing only IDs actually returned during the request. No fabricated grounding. Any model text including empty, malformed, repeated search requests or unsupported IDs must still result in valid shape; at most three search calls; if search returns nothing, do not invent evidence.

cards.title: BM25 retrieval boundary
cards.payload: Build a BM25 index and search ranked email documents using provided tokenizer; cover exact toy scores, empty and unknown queries, correct top-k ranking, recall and performance. Do not replace with a vector database merely because RAG literature describes one.

cards.title: Search-hop and support verifier
cards.payload: Use existing deterministic email-QA tests: positive grounded support shape; negative unknown support IDs, malformed outputs, search-loop overrun, and empty-result evidence. Live score remains NOT_RUN until genuinely measured.
